subject: Post-call recap: FinTechCo multi-region perf / next tests
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: FinTechCo multi-region perf / next tests

Hi Alex + Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side:

- Goal: validate multi-region latency & availability for your GenAI features (US/EU) and compare against your current hyperscaler endpoints.
- What we'll provide: test harness + sample payloads, short-running benchmark across us-east-1 and eu-west-1, plus a VPC/private run if you want an on-prem style comparison.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cold-start behavior, and error rate under a modest sustained load.
- Differentiators we'll surface: regional model variants, dedicated vs shared pools, prefix/KV cache behavior, and data residency/KMS controls.

Action items we agreed on:
1) Alex to confirm test windows and sample payloads (size distribution).
2) Redwood to share benchmark plan + security FAQ (I've attached the plan outline).
3) Loop in Marissa for competitive details and Sean for infra specifics.

Proposed times (your timezone): Jun 22 or Jun 24, 60-minute window each — which works best?

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex@fintechco.com>

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the clear plan. Jun 24 works better for us (morning preferred). A few clarifications from our side:

- Payloads: typical request is 512 tokens median, 1-2k tokens 90th percentile. We can provide a small sample corpus.
- Comparison targets: we want to see tests vs our existing Bedrock endpoints and Vertex AI (if possible) — specifically p99 under steady-state.
- Security: can you confirm data residency for EU requests (logs/metadata stay in-region) and whether you support customer-managed keys (we'll attach a short security questionnaire).

I've attached our security doc (security-questions.pdf). Priya will coordinate availability.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of ML Platforms, FinTechCo

Thanks Alex — Jun 24 morning confirmed. Quick answers and next steps below:

Security/data residency
- Logs & metadata: we can restrict audit logs and request logs to the region you choose for the test (us-east-1 or eu-west-1) and provide export copies for your audit.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) for encryption of model I/O at rest.

Competitive / perf notes (high level)
- Bedrock / Vertex: hyperscalers have broad regional presence, but they typically run on multi-tenant endpoints with less predictable tail latency under bursty loads.
- Redwood differentiators for this test: dedicated pools (predictable throughput), prefix/KV caching to reduce token cost and p95/p99 tail, and the ability to run identical configs in-hosted, dedicated, or private VPC modes.
- For multi-region: we'll spin up identical endpoints in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 and measure end-to-end latency from your clients (we recommend running the client-side probes from your infra as well to include network egress).

Benchmark plan & attachments
- Attached: redwood-multi-region-bench-plan.xlsx (plan + proposed payload distributions).
- We'll collect p50/p95/p99, cold vs warm behavior, throughput, and error rates over a 30-minute steady-state run and a 10-minute burst test.

Next steps
1) Priya to confirm Jun 24 09:00-10:00 ET (we'll assume that slot and adjust if needed).
2) Alex to send sample payloads and any additional endpoints to compare (Bedrock/Vertex URLs).
3) Marissa/Sean: we'll need a short runbook for the private VPC scenario — can you own infra setup?

Link to the shared benchmark doc: https://drive.google.com/fintechco/benchmark-plan

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
